\[
I_{\text{out}} = \begin{cases} 255 & I > t \\ 0 & I \le t \end{cases},\qquad t = 128
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(I\): The input value from 0 to 255
- \(t\): The threshold

Every pixel is compared with the same level t. The result is 255 where the value is above the threshold and 0 elsewhere, or the reverse with Invert. This is the basic global thresholding of Gonzalez and Woods. It works when objects and background have clearly different levels everywhere in the image.
